data.name: Leucine
data.description: Branched-chain essential amino acid and the best-characterised nutrient input to mTORC1. Free leucine binds Sestrin2, releasing the GATOR2 brake; a competing model has leucyl-tRNA synthetase as the sensor instead.
data.description_beginner: An essential amino acid and the best-understood dietary trigger for mTORC1. Free leucine binds to the sensor Sestrin2, releasing its brake on GATOR2; a rival idea says the real sensor is actually an enzyme called leucyl-tRNA synthetase (LARS) instead.

reading_levels.beginner: The amino acid the cell watches most closely.
reading_levels.student: Essential BCAA; its cytosolic concentration is read by Sestrin2 and (contested) by LARS.
reading_levels.research: Binds Sestrin2 with ~20 µM Kd – within the range over which intracellular leucine actually fluctuates, which is the main argument that Sestrin2 is a physiological sensor rather than a binder.

studies.title: Dynamic Visualization of mTORC1 Activity in Living Cells
studies.authors: Zhou X; Clister TL; Lowry PR; Seldin MM; Wong GW; Zhang J

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Mammalian cell lines (live-cell FRET imaging, subcellularly targeted reporter)
studies.finding: TORCAR, described by its authors as the first genetically encoded FRET reporter of mTORC1 activity, lets mTORC1 be watched in living cells as it changes. It showed mTORC1 activity not only at the lysosome but also in the cytosol, nucleus and at the plasma membrane; growth factor spread activity widely, while a leucine surrogate kept it at the lysosome and nucleus. A growth-factor-induced calcium transient contributed to mTORC1 activity. The earliest live reader of mTORC1 held in the atlas.

studies.title: Dynamics of mTORC1 activation in response to amino acids
studies.authors: Manifava M; Smith M; Rotondo S; Walker S; Niewczas I; Zoncu R; Clark J; Ktistakis NT

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: HEK293 cells; live imaging of RAPTOR and a fluorescent di-leucine analogue
studies.finding: Live imaging shows mTORC1 moves to lysosomes within 2 minutes of amino acid addition and peaks by 5 minutes, in step with leucine arriving in lysosomes; phosphorylation of classic mTORC1 targets lags behind, suggesting mTORC1 passes briefly through the lysosome before acting on substrates elsewhere.

studies.title: An SLC7A5-dependent nutrient-sensing circuit overcomes cisplatin tolerance via mTOR-autophagy signaling.
studies.authors: Rao P; Zhang T; Li Ju; Wei W; Xia X; Chen Q; Xu X; Feng X

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Human cancer cell lines (genome-wide CRISPR-Cas9 screen)
studies.finding: A genome-wide CRISPR screen found that mTOR inhibition promotes cisplatin tolerance by activating cytoprotective autophagy — the opposite of the canonical view. SLC7A5 integrates this mTOR-autophagy axis, and leucine supplementation resensitises SLC7A5-expressing tumour cells to cisplatin.

studies.title: D-Amino Acid Prodrug DLMEH Activates mTORC1 via Sestrin2 to Restore Muscle Protein Synthesis in Sarcopenia.
studies.authors: Shim JH; Lee JY; Ahn BK; Woo SW; Han J; Kim HS

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Rat (dexamethasone-induced muscle atrophy); human primary myotubes
studies.finding: DLMEH, a D-leucine ester prodrug, binds Sestrin2 with leucine-like potency (Kd 28.3 uM, equivalent to L-leucine) and activates mTORC1 in a Sestrin2-dependent way. It restored protein synthesis in human myotubes and preserved muscle mass, grip strength and endurance in a rat dexamethasone-induced atrophy model (not an ageing sarcopenia model).

studies.title: A systems study reveals concurrent activation of AMPK and mTOR by amino acids
studies.authors: Dalle Pezze P; Ruf S; Sonntag AG; Langelaar-Makkinje M; Hall P; Heberle AM; Razquin Navas P; van Eunen K; Tölle RC; Schwarz JJ; Wiese H; Warscheid B; Deitersen J; Stork B; Fäßler E; Schäuble S; Hahn U; Horvatovich P; Shanley DP; Thedieck K

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Human cell lines; amino acid re-addition time courses, quantitative proteomics and dynamic modelling
studies.finding: Adding amino acids back to starved cells switched on AMPK, PI3K and mTORC2 acutely and independently of mTORC1, at the same time as mTOR. AMPK activation ran through CaMKK-beta and, under amino acid sufficiency, AMPK kept autophagy going via ULK1. So the textbook picture of AMPK and mTORC1 as simple opposites does not hold in the first minutes after feeding - which matters for how the AMPK-ULK1 feedback arm behaves over time.

studies.title: Leucyl-tRNA synthetase controls TORC1 via the EGO complex
studies.authors: Bonfils G; Jaquenoud M; Bontron S; Ostrowicz C; Ungermann C; De Virgilio C

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Budding yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) genetics and biochemistry; LeuRS Cdc60 and EGO complex (Gtr1) interaction assays
studies.finding: In budding yeast, the leucyl-tRNA synthetase Cdc60 bound the Rag GTPase Gtr1, part of the EGO complex that activates TORC1, and this binding depended on leucine. The authors reported that the interaction was both necessary and sufficient to pass the leucine signal on to TORC1. When Cdc60 was busy editing wrongly charged tRNA(Leu), the interaction with Gtr1 was lost. The model is that TORC1 reads how well tRNA(Leu) is being charged as a stand-in for how much leucine the cell has. Together with Han et al. 2012 in human cells, it was one of the early papers to propose a tRNA synthetase as a leucine sensor upstream of the Rags. Boundary: Yeast only. The mammalian leucine sensor most widely accepted today is Sestrin2, and this yeast mechanism has not been reconciled with it. Drafted from the abstract only.

studies.title: Hypothalamic mTOR signaling regulates food intake
studies.authors: Cota D; Proulx K; Smith KA; Kozma SC; Thomas G; Woods SC; Seeley RJ

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Rats (Long-Evans): fasting/refeeding, intracerebroventricular leucine, leptin and rapamycin; hypothalamic immunostaining and Western blot
studies.finding: In rats, hypothalamic mTOR signalling (phosphorylated S6K1 and S6) changed with energy status in specific hypothalamic regions and was found in NPY and POMC neurons of the arcuate nucleus. Injecting leucine into the brain ventricles raised hypothalamic mTOR signalling and lowered food intake and body weight. Leptin also raised hypothalamic mTOR activity, and blocking mTOR with rapamycin in the brain blunted leptin's effect on reducing food intake. The authors proposed that hypothalamic mTOR acts as a fuel sensor linked to how much an animal eats. Boundary: rats, direct brain (intracerebroventricular) dosing, short-term food intake; drawn from the abstract only, so doses and effect sizes are not given here.

relations.mechanism: A competing model: the enzyme that loads leucine onto tRNA doubles as the leucine sensor, binding free leucine directly.
relations.mechanism_beginner: One competing idea: the enzyme that loads leucine onto its transport molecule for protein-building doubles as the leucine sensor.
relations.boundary: Proposed before the Sestrin2 model and never cleanly reconciled with it.
relations.note: CONTESTED with LEU-SESN2. Two published leucine sensors, both from strong labs, never resolved head-to-head. Prime Contradiction Engine seed.

relations.mechanism: Leucine binds a pocket inside Sestrin2 with roughly 20 uM affinity - close to the concentration at which cells actually feel leucine coming and going. The bound sensor can no longer hold GATOR2, so leucine effectively switches the brake off.
relations.mechanism_beginner: Leucine sticks to a pocket inside Sestrin2 and makes it let go of the next protein in line – that's how the cell notices leucine is around.
relations.boundary: Affinity was measured in vitro; whether the same 20 uM setpoint holds in tissues with different leucine transport is untested. VAL2025 (2025 cryo-EM) shows the leucine-induced shape change in Sestrin2 that releases GATOR2, again in purified protein and cultured cells. SHIM2026 is a 2026 rat study (dexamethasone-induced muscle atrophy, not an ageing model) with human myotubes; it tests a leucine-mimetic prodrug and supports Sestrin2-dependent mTORC1 activation, not the 20 uM leucine setpoint.
